units.title: Complete-edge-coloring bound from monochromatic-or-rainbow triangles
units.statement: In a complete graph with q edge colors, at least two used, and every triangle monochromatic or rainbow, each color component is a clique of size at most q-1. For a fixed vertex, each of q color classes contains at most q-2 neighbors, so there are at most (q-1)^2 vertices. When q-1 is prime, coloring pairs in the affine plane by line direction attains the bound. The 101-player, 11-score case therefore forces a triangle with exactly two equal scores.
steps: Show a path of two edges with one color closes to a same-color triangle
Use an outside vertex to bound a maximal color clique by q-1
Count neighbors of one vertex across q colors and construct equality by slopes
